key_insight: A hybrid-dimensional Biot formulation is solved on non-conforming fracture meshes by combining XFEM, Lagrange multipliers, and optimization-based domain decomposition to handle discontinuities in both displacement and pressure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to model coupled flow and deformation in fractured porous media without requiring mesh conformity to fractures, which is valuable for subsurface engineering and geomechanics.
method: XFEM allows 3D mesh elements to intersect fractures arbitrarily while representing displacement and pressure jumps.
Lagrange multipliers enforce displacement continuity and provide fracture traction/stress.
Fixed-stress splitting decouples flow and mechanics, and the mixed-dimensional pressure solve is accelerated with Conjugate Gradient.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the fixed-stress scheme combined with the CG solver is highly effective for this class of mixed-dimensional Biot problems, though no specific numerical benchmarks are given in the abstract.
watch_item: Implementation is nontrivial because it requires robust handling of XFEM discontinuities, Lagrange multiplier constraints, and optimization-based coupling on mixed-dimensional geometries.
paper_title: Hybrid-Dimensional Biot Problem with an Optimization Based Domain Decomposition Approach
